title: Mackenzie down the river to the Arctic Ocean, 1789
summary: Mackenzie left Fort Chipewyan on 3 June 1789 with French-Canadian voyageurs, a German and a party of Chipewyan guides led by a man called English Chief. They went by Great Slave Lake and the great river that now bears his name, and on 14 July reached the sea. He called it the River of Disappointment because it did not lead to the Pacific.

events.label: The Arctic Ocean, not the Pacific
events.text: He saw the tide and whales and took the sea for the Arctic Ocean. The river's name for the Dene is Deh Cho, the big river.
